title: The ternary Goldbach-Vinogradov theorem with almost equal Piatetski-Shapiro primes
abstract: A Lean 4 proof of Theorem 1 of Yanbo Song, The ternary Goldbach-Vinogradov theorem with almost equal Piatetski-Shapiro primes, arXiv 2012.06322 v1, 2020, with any positive margin in the window, by the deduction of Section 4 on page 9. Theorem 1 says that for 44/45 < gamma < 1 every large enough odd n is p1 + p2 + p3 with each pi a prime of the form floor of m to the power 1/gamma and |pi - n/3| <= y, for every y > n to the power 52 - 45 gamma over 8. The margin results rest on one cited input, the paper's Lemma 3, which is Theorem 3 of C. D. Pan and C. B. Pan, Goldbach Conjecture, Science Press, Beijing, 1988, taken at the exponent 7/8 as the explicit hypothesis Lemma3 7/8 and never as an axiom. From it the entry proves Theorem 1 for every window y > n to the power 52 - 45 gamma over 8 plus delta with delta > 0, and the page 9 asymptotic formula for R of n on the same windows; the paper's Lemmas 4 and 5 are proved. The exact window result also takes the transfer step of page 9 at the exact threshold, LogTransferDQ, as a second hypothesis. An independent check of the lab could not prove that transfer step at the exact threshold, since Lemma 4 holds with a loss of n to the epsilon only, so Theorem 1 at the exact window remains open here and the headline result is the margin version. Binary Goldbach is open and is not claimed; ternary Goldbach is a theorem of Helfgott 2013. AI agents wrote the Lean code, as listed in PORTING.md, and it is offered for human audit.
